messages:
Maya S.: Hey team — prepping the Acme POC private deploy. Customer wants guidance on connectivity. Quick list of asks:
1) Preserve client source IP for backend logs/tracing?
2) Exact firewall/egress ports and CIDRs for PrivateLink vs peering?
3) How does TLS inspection affect mTLS to our connector?
4) Any pricing differences for PrivateLink vs public API, and Dedicated egress billing?

Alex W.: Short answers: PrivateLink terminates at our ENI and we will see the endpoint IP; original client IP is NOT preserved at TCP layer unless you proxy-forward it. For true source-IP preservation use peering/TGW or run a passthrough proxy.

Priya (SE): Port/CIDR snippet for your network team:
```
- PrivateLink ENIs (example): 10.12.34.0/26 TCP 443
- VPC peering route (example): 10.100.0.0/16 TCP 443
- DNS: UDP/TCP 53 -> if using our DNS stub endpoints
- NTP: UDP 123 -> for clock sync (optional)
- Healthchecks: TCP 443/80 -> optional
```
Note: we do TLS on 443. If your org performs TLS inspect, you need to either establish mTLS from your proxy to our connector or avoid terminating the client cert chain.

Jordan - Acme NetOps: We must do TLS inspection for outbound traffic. If we terminate and re-encrypt, will that break customer-side mTLS to Redwood?

Alex W.: Yes — TLS inspection that terminates the original client cert will break end-to-end mTLS. Options: (a) Peering/TGW preserves TCP so mTLS remains intact, (b) configure your proxy to present a cert we trust for proxy->Redwood mTLS and pass a client identity header for logs, or (c) do application-layer forwarding (reverse proxy) that injects X-Forwarded-For.

Maya S.: Cost question from procurement: does PrivateLink add any Redwood-side data processing or surcharge?

Priya (SE): PrivateLink itself is billed by cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) for the interface endpoint. On Redwood: hosted usage (tokens/embeddings) billed per our normal rates. For Dedicated we charge reserved capacity; enterprise contracts may itemize egress separately. I'll escalate to billing to confirm specific line items for the POC.

infra-bot: @Maya S. created INF-3421 to confirm ENI CIDR ranges and Dedicated egress policy.

Maya S.: Next steps: Priya to confirm exact ENI ranges and provide an official SG/NACL example; Alex to write short doc on patterns (preserve IP vs app headers); billing to confirm any extra egress lines. Jordan, can you confirm whether peering/TGW is possible in your org? :thumbsup:

Jordan - Acme NetOps: Peering is allowed but our default is PrivateLink. We'll check whether we can create a passthrough for certs or allow proxy mTLS to Redwood.

Priya (SE): I'll drop a one-pager + SG rules by EOD and include the example curl and sample X-Forwarded-For header.

Alex W.: Also flag: if you need zero-translation for observability, TGW + static routes is the cleanest. PrivateLink is best for isolation but expect to translate source IP at the ENI level.

Maya S.: Awesome — thanks. Filing followups in INF-3421 and looping in billing and security reviewers.
